# Radiology Monster (radiology.monster)

> Radiology Monster (radiology.monster) is made by Horalix (https://horalix.com), a medical AI company in Sarajevo. Real cases. Deeper understanding. Radiology Monster is a radiology reading workstation in the browser for medical students and residents: real CT, MRI, X-ray, mammography and ultrasound studies, where you scroll the whole study, mark what you see and are graded against the expert reference on the exact slice, with each task linked to the page of Learning Radiology (Herring, 5th ed.) that explains it.

Also written: radiology.monster, RadiologyMonster, Radiology.Monster. Official site: https://www.radiology.monster/

## Who makes it

- Radiology Monster is made by Horalix (https://horalix.com), a medical AI company in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina. Horalix builds AI for medical imaging, including an AI-assisted echocardiography workflow for clinician review.
- Horalix's AI drew the anatomy layer in Radiology Monster, labelled AI wherever it appears. The findings that grade answers come from each image collection's own experts.
- About page, with the image collections and their licences: https://www.radiology.monster/about
- Contact: support@horalix.com, or @radiology.monster on Instagram.

## What it offers

- 600+ real, de-identified patients and 1,700+ image tasks across CT, MRI, X-ray, mammography and ultrasound, from public research collections whose licences allow reuse (Creative Commons, NIH).
- Learn, Practice, Assess and Review modes; marking tools; deterministic grading against the experts' own outlines and boxes (a mark must land on the finding, on the right slice and side).
- An anatomy layer naming the organs, vessels, bones and airways on every scan, an anatomy atlas, anatomy drills with spaced repetition, on-call shifts and a search-pattern coach.
- Certificates in three levels (Foundation, Intermediate, Advanced) for each body area (chest, abdomen and pelvis, neuro, musculoskeletal, breast) and for the whole library (General Radiology). Each level is an exam, taken in order, and each is a real step up: Foundation 15 untimed questions, pass mark 70%; Intermediate 25 questions at 3 minutes each, pass mark 80%, at least half of them marking the finding on the image, no two-answer questions; Advanced 40 questions at 2 minutes each, pass mark 90% with no half points, mostly marked on the image, subtle cases first (the whole library: 30, 50 and 75 questions). No hints, every answer graded against the expert reference, and the result after the last question. Each certificate has a public check page and can be added to LinkedIn under Licenses & certifications.
- Progress follows the account: every submitted answer is saved to the learner's account with its grade and appears on any device after sign-in, and the browser keeps a copy for when the connection drops. One device is signed in at a time.
- Classes for professors: a class page with one join link to share. Students join after seeing what the professor can follow (study days, exam results and certificates, never answers or payments) and can leave at any time.
- For education and practice only: not a medical device, not for clinical decisions, and its certificates are not a medical qualification.

## Prices

- Free account: two sample patients in the full workstation, with grading. No card needed.
- Monthly: $20 every 30 days. Yearly: $150 every 365 days ($12.50 a month).
- Students: 30% off with an eligible university email (including .edu, .edu.ba and .ac.uk): $14 every 30 days or $105 every 365 days.
- Payments by Whop; cancel future renewals at any time from Billing.

## Credits

- Anatomy outlines: AI, by Horalix, the company that makes Radiology Monster. Thanks to Horalix.com (https://horalix.com), every structure in the anatomy layer is marked. It has not been reviewed by a radiologist. Only the collections' expert references grade case answers and exams; anatomy drills also use the AI outlines, marked AI.
- Findings: the reference annotations published with each image collection, made by its radiologists and clinicians or under their supervision; every case names its source and licence.
- Radiology Monster is not affiliated with or endorsed by the publisher or authors of Learning Radiology.
